decision: Build approach D: a first-class Tiller.Mutation vocabulary across 5 axes (whitelist, result override, driver swap, injected latency, process kill), N-way concurrent fork race under DynamicSupervisor, LiveView inspector, and automatic first-divergence plus smallest-decisive-mutation analysis.
rationale: Chosen over C (single whitelist axis, recommended), A (vertical slice), B (event core first). Effort XL, risk High, accepted knowingly. Only version that makes the screen an instrument rather than a spectacle. Foundation is 250-400 lines (revised up from a 30-line estimate after Codex verified spawn_subagent blocks at actions.ex:52): cast-based session loop, attributed ordered event store replacing the global list, Phoenix.PubSub, Replay driver with recorded-result injection. Documented fallback to approach C if the 30-minute divergence-detection spike fails.

decision: Integrate tiller with open-seed as an MCP client of the engine (option 1): Tiller.Seed speaks JSON-RPC to `seed mcp serve`, Tiller.Tools gains seed_* port verbs, root sessions hold the worker verbs and subagents only the reads; operator verbs are on no whitelist. Options 2 (tiller as a seed-harness adapter), 3 (tiller as Seed's trajectory instrument), and 4 (open-seed as tiller's template) are recorded in docs/designs/open-seed-integration.md and deferred.
rationale: Needs no LLM driver, respects open-seed's rule that only the port touches a store, and gives tiller real tools with distinct failure modes (the port's exit classes: 2 contention, 3 invalid transition, 6 fenced out) which the butterfly lab lists as its next step. Option 2 is blocked on a real driver (FakeDriver would duplicate scripts/harness/mock); option 3 on the async/attributed event core plus persistence; option 4 only pays off with multiple agents on tiller.

decision: Divergence spike passed: approach D (full butterfly lab) is GO. Tiller.Divergence.first_diff/2 is a prefix walk with a normalizing equality projection; Tiller.Event defined with from_log/2.
rationale: A branch forked at turn N shares its parent's first N events by construction, so first divergence is prefix comparison, not alignment. The only decision was the equality projection: pids, refs, ports, funs, and stack traces are erased by default; key: overrides. Under 20 lines of logic, 8 tests, well inside the 30-minute box the design set as the go/no-go.

decision: Butterfly lab foundation (steps 2 to 6) landed: async cast-based Session with await/2 on State.subscribe/1, attributed Tiller.Event store with global seq, non-blocking spawn_subagent, Tiller.Mutation type. Step 2 (real tools) is met by the seed_* verbs. State.subscribe/1 uses Registry, not Phoenix.PubSub, until the LiveView step adds Phoenix.
rationale: Registry gives the same {:tiller_event, event} delivery with zero dependencies; adding Phoenix for PubSub alone before there is a LiveView would be premature and the seam (State.subscribe/1) hides the swap. A tool cannot GenServer.call its own session, so the session id a tool needs comes from the process dictionary (Session.current_id/0).

decision: Open question 2 answered: Tiller.Driver gets an optional resume_ctx(initial_ctx, replayed_events) callback; the replay driver calls it once at hand-off, and a driver without it is used with the context supplied at fork time. Steps 7 and 8 landed: Tiller.Driver.Replay ({:replay, action, result, ctx} reply shape, origin: :replay on events), Session.fork/4 over whitelist, driver, result_override, latency; kill_at refused; Tiller.Lab.race/4 as the MVP without the screen.
rationale: Contexts are opaque, so only the driver can rebuild one; asking the driver with its initial context plus the replayed events works for a script (drop N) and for a conversation (append N turns). Injecting recorded results rather than re-running actions is what makes replay deterministic and side-effect free (verified: a replayed spawn_subagent creates no child). Overrides on the replay path made result_override free, and a per-turn delay made latency free, so four axes ship instead of the two the MVP required.

decision: Step 9 landed: TillerWeb.LabLive, one page with timeline, turn detail, and live race panes; State.subscribe/1 now on Phoenix.PubSub; Phoenix kept to phoenix, phoenix_live_view, phoenix_pubsub, bandit, jason (lazy_html in test), with the client JS served from the packages' priv/static and no asset pipeline. Butterfly lab MVP is met.
rationale: The page only needs a LiveSocket and server-rendered HEEx, so esbuild, node, and Ecto would be weight without function; Plug.Static over deps' priv/static serves the two bundles the layout needs. Live divergence per branch treats a shorter, still-running branch as identical so far, which is the only reading that does not flash a false divergence at every turn.

decision: Open question 5 answered and kill_at built: a supervisor restart IS a resume because a session's start arguments are an identity, not a state. The packet (origin driver and ctx, whitelist, latency, lineage) is written to Tiller.State at start; on restart init/1 finds it and starts <id>/r<n> forked from the dead session at its death turn via the replay driver. Kill branches are restart: :transient; others stay :temporary. Tiller.Supervisor runs with max_restarts: 100. All five mutation axes are live.
rationale: Keeps DynamicSupervisor's native restart instead of an external resurrector, and reuses fork/replay/resume_ctx unchanged. Verified in the strongest form: a branch killed before turn 2 resumes and ends identical to its parent, and a second kill resumes again from the latest log. The default restart intensity (3 in 5s) tripped on a single race and took every resumed session down, hence the wide valve.

decision: Open question 3 decided: rank mutations within an axis by Mutation.size/1 and across axes by divergence turn (later diverging is the smaller change to the run); same turn on different axes ties; branches that never diverged are unranked. Never compare sizes across axes. Lab.race sets rank; ranked/1, smallest/1, format/1 and the race table use it.
rationale: Axes are incommensurable and any cross-axis weight would be invented. The divergence turn is a property of the trajectory every branch shares, already computed, and reads as how much of the run survived the mutation. Dense ranks make ties honest; the weights alternative remains possible as an option if a total order is ever needed.
